chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Remember that pleasures will pass away while the consequences will stay.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of remembering the transience of pleasures in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the dialectic between fleeting sensory gratification and the permanent spiritual or karmic 'debts' (tabi'at) that follow. This teaching underscores the Shia ethical emphasis on mindfulness (muraqaba), urging believers to prioritize enduring moral consequences over temporary worldly distractions. It serves as a practical guide for self-accountability, reminding the faithful that every action leaves an indelible mark on the soul.
